text:
olivia: Heads-up — FinLedger asked for a per-customer routing bypass for a short window. They say their compliance KYC checks must hit a node in eu-west-1 for jurisdictional reasons. Can we discuss guardrails?

sam: What's the exact ask? Full bypass to dedicated pool or just route affinity to eu-west-1?

olivia: Affinity + guaranteed path. They want requests with header X-FINLEDGER-ID to always route to the eu-west-1 path, bypassing cost-optimized fallback. TTL = 72h initially.

kevin: Requiring bypass sounds risky. We need audit trail, a kill-switch, and quota limits. Also prefer a scoped escape (only endpoints matching /v1/kyc/*).

maya: Agree with Kevin. UX idea: a console flow where SEs submit: org, header pattern, route target, TTL, reason, owner. Then Auto-approver for low-risk requests, manual for >X qps or >30d TTL.

sam: For telemetry, add a per-org metric tag and a routed-path label so we can measure p95 latency and cost delta. We'll also need alerts if traffic to bypassed route > committed quota.

olivia: Can we sketch a minimum policy payload? I mocked this in Slack:

```
policy: {
  org: "finledger",
  match: { header: "X-FINLEDGER-ID", prefix: "" },
  path_match: "/v1/kyc/*",
  action: "route:eu-west-1:dedicated-pool-3",
  ttl: "72h",
  quota: "1000rps",
  auditor: "ops@redwood.ai"
}
```

kevin: That looks fine. Add an explicit fallback policy: what happens when eu-west-1 is unhealthy? auto-fail to nearest region or block? For compliance, they may require block. Need customer-specified fallback field.

maya: Exactly — add fallback: { type: "block" | "fallback-to: eu-central-1" }. Also record "approved_by" and approval timestamp in audit log.

sam: Implementation notes: gateway routing table will accept a new rule type 'org-scoped' with precedence > default routing. We should also ensure rules are rate-limited by org and model to avoid noisy-neighbor.

ops-bot: deployment queued for service: routing-config (sha: a1b2c3). ETA ~30m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

olivia: Approval? @kevin @maya please ack if you approve the console + audit requirements. I want to avoid ad-hoc manual config changes.

kevin: ack. Approve with conditions: TTL <= 30d without exec-level signoff, fallback must be explicit, and quota enforced.

maya: ack. Also require a one-click revoke in the UI and an API endpoint to list active org-scoped routes.

sam: I'll add telemetry tags: redwood.org.override=true, redwood.override.reason=finledger-kyc. Will emit metrics: override.requests, override.denied, override.fallbacks.

olivia: Thanks. I'll draft the console request form and the signed policy payload for legal. We should also add a post-approval audit summary email to ops-channel.

deploy-bot: routing-config deployed to canary. Check /canary/routing/status for live metrics.

sam: Quick follow-up — how do we handle header spoofing? If X-FINLEDGER-ID is easy to fake we must require token binding or mutual TLS from their integration. Add a note in the request flow that we need an ingestion auth method.

olivia: Good point. I'll add required integration: mTLS or signed JWT per org.

kevin: OK. After the console prototype, let's run a tabletop rollback drill: simulate eu-west outage and confirm block vs fallback behaves as policy says.

maya: I'll create the ticket for the console flow + audit logs + revoke button. Tagging infra and telemetry.

olivia: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll post the draft policy and a short runbook once ticket is up. :white_check_mark:
